messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: PrivateConnect EUC2 (eu-central-2) — significant route churn observed for customer cust-acme-prod. Multiple BGP withdraws from peer <peer-123>. Impact: intermittent connectivity to PrivateLink endpoints in eu-central-2. Paging on-call.

alice-ops: acked. I'm oncall for infra. Kicking off triage. Anyone seeing related SLO pages? @bob-netops can you pull BGP session state?

bob-netops: looking. Saw repeated BGP NOTIFICATION on one session, then flaps. Running `show ip bgp neighbors peer-123` now.

bob-netops: ```
BGP neighbor is 10.10.20.1, remote AS 64512
  BGP state = Established, up for 00:15:23
  Last error: NOTIFICATION received, code 3 / subcode 1
  Received 18 updates in the last 120s, 12 withdrawn prefixes
```

bob-netops: also traceroute from gw-euc2-azb to cust-private-endpoint shows paths alternating between transit-a and transit-b.

carla-sre: I can see increased 5xxs on the PrivateLink healthcheck metrics for cust-acme-prod. From the dashboard: 15m error rate jumped to 6% (baseline 0.2%). Potentially customer-facing. @dylan-support can you confirm if the customer is seeing impact?

dylan-support: customer called into support at 20:47 UTC reporting intermittent timeouts when connecting to their internal endpoint. They flagged spikes around 20:40–20:50. They're asking if we have an ETA. I told them we're investigating and will update in 15.

emma-eng: quick note — our smart routing policy should have failed over to the alternate region after N seconds, but this looks like within-region instability affecting PrivateLink connectivity. Could be route withdrawal loop on provider side.

alice-ops: timeline: initial withdraws start 20:44 UTC. I want a temporary mitigation: suppress the flapping path at our edge and pin traffic to the more stable transit. @bob-netops can you prep a route-map to prefer transit-b and dampen the flapping prefixes? Keep in mind we need small blast radius.

bob-netops: prepping route-map now. Proposal:
```
route-map PREFER-TRANSIT-B permit 10
 set ip next-hop 10.20.30.5
!
route-map DAMPEN-FLAP deny 10
 match ip address prefix-list CUST-ACME
 set local-preference 200
```
Will test on a single AZ (euc2-azb) before rolling.

carla-sre: FYI I'm ready to open canary and monitor. Will watch tail of logs and KV cache hit ratios. If we see >1% 5xx after change, rollback immediately.

alice-ops: go ahead on canary. @sam-custsuccess please post a short customer-facing update: we're mitigating route churn and investigating root cause, ETA 30m.

sam-custsuccess: posting now to cust-acme support channel: "We're seeing transient routing instability affecting PrivateLink in eu-central-2; team is applying a targeted routing preference to stabilize traffic. We'll follow up with a detailed update in 30 minutes." :white_check_mark:

bob-netops: applied route-map to euc2-azb edge (canary). Monitoring BGP updates and data plane.

bob-netops: initial result: withdraws on peer-123 stopped on that edge, BGP UPDATE count dropped to normal. Traceroutes now consistently via transit-b. (:+1: reaction)

carla-sre: canary metrics: 5xx dropped from 6% -> 0.8% after 90s. KV cache evictions unchanged. Good signal.

dylan-support: relaying to customer: "We've applied a targeted route preference in your region which appears to have stabilized connectivity. Please confirm on your side." They replied: "We're seeing connectivity back for most services, some short reconnects but overall better." They also asked whether we saw any data plane packet loss.

emma-eng: I pulled flow logs — small spike in retransmits around 20:42–20:46, then normal. Looks like provider-side BGP instability, not our infra.

alice-ops: ok next: escalate to transit provider NOC. @bob-netops open ticket with full bgp dump and traceroutes, include AS path and timestamps. Also prepare rollback plan to remove route-map if any side-effects appear.

bob-netops: ticket created with provider (ticket #TN-99823). Included BGP RIB, update timestamps, and the `show ip route` and `traceroute` outputs. Provider acknowledged and is investigating.

carla-sre: scheduling post-incident eval. Assigning action items: 1) improve early detection on abnormal withdraw rate (bob), 2) add automated quick-canary route preference script (emma), 3) confirm cust comms (sam). I'll create follow-ups in the incidents board.

alice-ops: oncall handoff in 20 minutes. @carla-sre will take primary; I'm marking my status as 'handoff' at 21:07 UTC.

carla-sre: taking over primary oncall. @alice-ops thanks for initial triage. I'll keep monitoring and reach out to provider NOC if TN-99823 takes longer than 45m.

alice-ops: handing off. Notes: canary applied to euc2-azb only. If provider announces fix, we should remove route-map and let smart routing rebalance. If error rate creeps up, remove route-map first, then escalate.

bob-netops: provider confirmed seeing misconfiguration on their iBGP reflector causing route re-advertises -> withdraws. They pushed a fix at 21:05 UTC and are monitoring.

dylan-support: customer reports full recovery at 21:10 UTC. Marking customer impact as "intermittent connectivity" with duration ~26 minutes (20:44–21:10). Logged in support ticket.

carla-sre: final check: BGP updates normal across all edges, healthchecks stable, 5xx back to baseline. Closing incident thread, creating postmortem draft with timeline and action items.

alice-ops: thanks team. Follow-ups: bob to add automated bgp-withdraw alert, emma to prototype route-stabilizer script, sam to send customer wrap-up email with RCA timeline. :raised_hands:

incident-bot: Incident P1 (privconnect-euc2-route-surge) resolved by operator action and provider fix. Duration 00:26:00. Links: incident-docs/privconnect-euc2-2623456789, ticket TN-99823.
